Create the z3guide-docs-bot GitHub App

This page uses GitHub's App-manifest flow to create the App in your personal account with the exact least-privilege permissions below. No webhook, no extra scopes.

Repository permissions requested:
  • Metadata: Read-only (mandatory)
  • Contents: Read & write — push the automation/update-z3-parameters branch
  • Pull requests: Read & write — open/update the parameter-update pull request
Account/org permissions: none. Issues: none. Webhook: disabled. Visibility: private (only on your account).
Sign in to github.com in this browser first. GitHub silently discards the manifest on an anonymous request and then reports Invalid GitHub App configuration — "url" wasn't supplied. That message means signed out; it does not mean the manifest is wrong. (Verified: posting this exact manifest without a session reproduces it.)

Open github.com/settings/apps/new in a new tab to check — if you get the Register new GitHub App form you are signed in and can come back here; if you get a sign-in page, sign in there first.

  1. Confirm you are signed in, using the link above.
  2. Click the button below. GitHub shows a confirmation page pre-filled from the manifest — review it and click Create GitHub App.
  3. GitHub redirects to your Apps list. Open z3guide-docs-bot → click Generate a private key (downloads a .pem), and copy the Client ID and the numeric App ID. You need both later.

Tip: to create it directly inside an organization instead, change the form action to https://github.com/organizations/<org>/settings/apps/new. Microsoft OSPO asks you to create it on your personal account first, then request the transfer to the target org through microsoft/github-operations. The manifest embedded above is kept in sync with manifest.json.
